title: Talent Sprint Q3 2026 — Hiring plan, interview rubrics, onboarding checklist (WIP)
content:
Context:
This is a working doc for the people-ops recruiting sprint targeting Q3 2026 hires. Primary goals: accelerate fill time for high-priority roles, tighten interviewer calibration to reduce variance, and standardize week-0 to week-12 onboarding for engineering and SRE hires. Draft format — notes, rubrics, and checklist items to iterate with hiring managers and hiring committee.

Summary goals (high level):
- Hire 10 IC engineers (mix infra/runtime/reliability) and 4 senior platform/SRE engineers between 2026-07-01 and 2026-09-30.
- Reduce time-to-offer from 40d -> 28d for priority tracks.
- Achieve panel calibration score variance <= 0.6 stddev (post-calibration baseline needed).
- All new hires to reach first-production-deploy milestone within 12 weeks where role-appropriate.

Prioritized roles (Q3 focus):
1) Serving Runtime Engineer (L4-L5) — 4 hires (high urgency)
2) Site Reliability Engineer, Platform (L5) — 2 hires
3) Developer Experience Engineer (L4) — 2 hires
4) Product Designer (L4) — 1 hire
5) Senior Program Manager (technical launches) — 1 hire

Hiring timeline (proposed cadence):
- Week A (immediately): Create role-specific scorecards + job postings. Owner: Hiring manager + Aisha (due 2026-01-19).
- Week A+1: Panel assignment and interviewer training session (1.5 hr). Owner: People Ops (Priya).
- Ongoing: Weekly pipeline review with hiring managers (Tues 10am PT).

Headcount snapshot (text table):
- Budgeted: 12 (Q3 allotment)
- Open reqs: 9 now (serving runtime 4, SRE 2, dev-ex 2, PM 1)
- Passive targets (sourcing): 60 active prospects across roles

Sourcing channels: internal referrals (priority), Hired, LinkedIn Recruiter, Diversity job boards (Techqueria / LesbiansWhoTech / WomenWhoCode), targeted outreach to relevant OSS contributors. Referral bonus reminder: still active for Q1 hires (confirm budget).

Interview rubric (single-page canonical — adapt per role):
Scoring scale: 1-5 (1 = missing / poor, 3 = meets bar, 5 = exceeds by wide margin). Use decimals for nuance (e.g., 3.5).
Core dimensions (applies to engineers):
- Technical depth (systems, algorithms, data structures) — can reason about tradeoffs for large models and inference scale (30% weight)
- Problem decomposition & debugging (20%)
- Runtime/infra judgement (designs for latency, batching, cache) (20%)
- Collaboration & communication (10%)
- Ownership / product sense (10%)
- Culture & signal alignment (diversity/equity mindset, 10%)

Sample rubric items per stage:
- Screen (30m): breadth assessment, basic system design problem, culture fit quick questions. Passing threshold: >=3.0 average across mandatory dims.
- Take-home (optional for senior): 72-hr exercise, evaluate approach and clarity, not just working code.
- Onsite (virtual): 3 interviews (deep system design, debugging pair, behavioral/hiring manager). Panel score = weighted average. Offer threshold: >=3.3 and no single category below 2.5 without documented mitigation.

Calibration notes (for interviewers):
- Mandatory 90-min calibration for all interviewers participating in Q3 sprint. Agenda: scoring guide walkthrough, 3 sample candidate recordings (anonymized), group scoring and discussion. Priya to schedule.
- For panels with mixed seniority, ensure at least one interviewer has recent hiring experience and documented calibration completion.

Interview panel templates (roles):
- Serving Runtime Engineer panel:
  1) Systems design (50m) — owner: Senior Runtime Eng
  2) Debugging/pair (40m) — owner: SRE
  3) Leadership/behavior + product sense (30m) — owner: hiring manager
- SRE panel:
  1) Incident debugging / postmortem reasoning (45m)
  2) Capacity & reliability design (45m)
  3) Cross-team collaboration & SLAs (30m)

Scorecard quick template (to paste into ATS):
- Candidate: NAME
- Role: ROLE
- Interviewers: NAMES
- Technical depth: X.X
- Problem decomposition: X.X
- Runtime judgement: X.X
- Communication: X.X
- Ownership/product: X.X
- Culture fit: X.X
- Overall recommendation: Strong hire / Hire / No hire / Hire w/ caveats
- Notes (concise): bullet points

Onboarding checklist (Week 0 to Week 12) — standardized baseline (tailor with hiring manager):
Pre-day 0 (people-ops action items):
- Offer paperwork signed, direct deposit, tax forms completed. Owner: People Ops
- Access request submitted (VPC, Slack, GitHub, internal dashboards). Owner: IT 
- Hardware order placed (spec: M1-Pro equivalent default unless otherwise requested). Owner: Ops procurement

Day 0–7 (orientation & setup):
- Orientation session (company mission, OKRs, product overview) — 2 hrs. Owner: People Ops
- Team onboarding (intro to team, tech stack, first buddy assigned) — 1 hr. Owner: hiring manager
- Local infra walkthrough: dev environment, repo map, runbook index, daily standup cadence. Owner: mentor/buddy
- First small task: fix a low-risk bug or docs improvement. Deliverable: PR merged. Owner: mentor

Week 2–4 (ramp):
- Deeper system reads + architecture deep-dive meeting with runtime team.
- Shadow on-call rotation and pager triage (read-only first).
- 1:1 with hiring manager to align 30/60/90 goals.

Week 5–12 (project & autonomy ramp):
- Own a mid-sized ticket that touches production infra (goal: feature or bug with infra review).
- Conduct a short retrospective on onboarding experience (submit to People Ops).
- Final ramp milestone: first production deploy or leading a post-deploy verification.

Role-specific addenda:
- SRE new hire: must pass on-call readiness checklist by week 8 (pager playbook walkthrough, runbook contributions).
- Runtime engineer: deliver 1 optimization proposal (latency or cost) in first 12 weeks.

Evaluation & success metrics for onboarding program:
- New hire NPS (post-90d) target >= 8/10.
- Time to first merged PR: median <= 21 days.
- Fraction meeting 12-week milestone: target >= 80%.

Diversity & inclusion notes:
- Blind resume step for initial triage where possible.
- Diverse-slate goal for every interview loop (at least one underrepresented candidate in final onsite slate).

Open questions / unresolved decisions (action items):
- Confirm budget for referral bonuses Q3 — Finance contact: Marcus Lee (action: Marcus to confirm by 2026-01-20).
- Decide whether take-home exercises are required for L5 roles (pros/cons list needed). Owner: Hiring com (due 2026-01-26).
- Define concrete calibration metric and how we measure variance baseline (data owner: Evan).

Next steps & owners (short):
- Finalize job descriptions (Aisha + hiring managers) — due 2026-01-19.
- Schedule interviewer calibration sessions (Priya) — invite out by 2026-01-15.
- Post role on prioritized channels (Aisha / sourcing) — 2026-01-20.

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep take-home limited to 48–72 hrs; heavy take-homes hurt conversion.
- Emphasize collaborative debugging in interviews (pair-programming), not solo whiteboarding.
- Track scorecard metadata in ATS to enable later analysis on panel variance.

Appendix: quick links to reference docs (copy into Confluence):
- Recruiting playbook: CONFLUENCE:RECRUIT-PLAYBOOK-101
- Onboarding survey template: CONFLUENCE:ONBOARD-SURVEY-202
- Old calibration notes: CONFLUENCE:CALIB-2024

End of doc — mark-up required: please add role-specific tweaks, especially for design and PM tracks.
